clubs_p: As the country moves club activities out of schools and into the community, this page lists what children in this district can take part in right now — school clubs and community clubs side by side, school by school.
clubs_s1_box: What the national government has set out: On 22 December 2025 the Japan Sports Agency and MEXT adopted the “Comprehensive Guidelines on Club Activity Reform and the Promotion of Community Club Activities”, under which a “reform implementation period” begins in FY2026.
clubs_s1_h: Moving Club Activities into the Community<small>部活動の地域移行とは</small>
clubs_s1_lead: A nationwide effort to move club activities, long run by teachers, over to community clubs and organisations. In the Shinooka district this happens at the same time as the school reorganisation, so this page shows both together.
clubs_s1_open1: We have not found any published material from Komaki City on when or how it will carry out this shift.
clubs_s1_open2: Which clubs the new schools will have after the reorganisation has not been announced.
clubs_s1_open3: The community clubs listed here have not been designated to take over any club activity.
clubs_s1_p1: Club activities have until now been run inside schools. With fewer children making clubs hard to sustain, and with the load on teachers, the direction set out is to shift weekend activities step by step to community clubs.
clubs_s1_p2: In the Shinooka district the schools are to be reorganised in FY2027. What happens to club activities afterwards, and how far community clubs will take them on, has not been announced.
clubs_s1_src: Source: Japan Sports Agency / MEXT, “Comprehensive Guidelines on Club Activity Reform and the Promotion of Community Club Activities” (adopted and published 22 December 2025)
clubs_s2_h: By School<small>学校ごとの部活動と地域クラブ</small>
clubs_s2_lead: Grouped by the schools as they are named today. We will keep using this grouping even after the reorganisation. School clubs come from each school’s own pages; community clubs from each club’s own posts.
clubs_s2_note: * Few schools publish a full list of their clubs. Only those we could confirm on each school’s pages or school diary are shown, so clubs are missing.
clubs_s3_h: Across the District<small>校区をまたぐ・市内全域の活動</small>
clubs_s3_lead: Activities not tied to one school district, open to children from across the city. Some are based in a neighbouring city but within reach of this district.
clubs_s4_box: Where this comes from: Club details are taken from what each club publishes itself (Instagram, websites), as far as we could read them. School clubs were confirmed on each school’s pages and school diary. The Komaki City Sports Association classes come from the association’s own listing. The Komaki boys’ and girls’ choir comes from the Komaki Music Federation’s member listing, and the programming classes from each class’s own website.
clubs_s4_h: About This List<small>このページの情報について</small>
clubs_s4_n1: Eligible school years, days and fees differ by club. Always confirm the current terms with the club.
clubs_s4_n2: This site does not recommend any club. The order of listing has no meaning.
clubs_s4_n3: There are activities not listed here. If you know of one we have missed, please let us know.
clubs_tg_e1_j3_city: Primary year 1 to junior high year 3 (Komaki residents)
clubs_tokadai_bb: In the school diaries, baseball enters tournaments as a combined team named “Tokadai” (桃花台野球部 / 桃花台チーム).
contact_rel_h: Who to Contact<small>関係する部署の問い合わせ先</small>
contact_rel_lead: These are the city, prefectural and national offices responsible for what this page covers. The numbers are the ones each office publishes (as of September 2026).
contact_rel_note: ※ Office names are left in Japanese, because that is the name you show at a counter or say on the phone. Names and numbers can change when the organisation is restructured. This site has no connection with any of these offices, and you do not need to mention it when you contact them.
